successors.name: Goguryeo
successors.text: Buyeo's core in northern Manchuria on the Songhua: between the Ashi River stronghold (Harbin) and Nong'an; the 3rd-century Records of the Three Kingdoms give 'an area some two thousand li square' and…

ledger.x: c. 2nd century BCE: Buyeo appears in northern Manchuria. 'The exact founding year of Buyeo is unclear'; it probably coexisted with Old Chosŏn and Jin and predated the Four Commanderies; infobox 'c. 2nd century BCE-494 CE'. -200 is a bridge for 'c. 2nd century BCE'.
86 BCE: Hae Buru founds Eastern Buyeo.
286: Buyeo is restored with Jin help.
c. February 347: Former Yan attacks Buyeo. 'c. February 347: Murong Huang of Former Yan attacked, and King Hyeon (玄) was captured.' A Goguryeo attack earlier had already caused 'further decline'.
348: the Yan campaign is taken to have ended by then (bridge).
494: the Buyeo court surrenders to Goguryeo.

wars.name: Buyeo and Eastern Han
wars.outcome: Buyeo is a nominal tributary and ally of the Eastern Han from 49; it raids Han holdings in 111, is restored to alliance in 120, sends troops to Xuantu against Goguryeo c.

wars.name: Murong Xianbei invasion of Buyeo
wars.outcome: Murong Hui's invasion kills King Uiryeo and drives the court to Okjeo; Emperor Wu of Jin helps Uira revive Buyeo.

wars.name: Former Yan attack on Buyeo
wars.outcome: c. February 347 Murong Huang's attack captures King Hyeon.

wars.name: Goguryeo conquest of Eastern Buyeo
wars.outcome: Gwanggaeto conquers the eastern refugee state.

wars.name: Wuji attack on Buyeo
wars.outcome: A Wuji (Mohe) attack drives the court to surrender to Goguryeo.

certainty.note: Steppe-forest frontier of northern Manchuria; the pages give no boundary, only the Records of the Three Kingdoms' size.
